claims.text: The rider's claim is that the route was far longer than quoted. The trip record and the GPS trace both establish the excess: the trace measures 19.71 km against a booked optimal of 14.6 km, an excess of 5.11 km and 35.00%, which clears both POL-RD-01 establishment tests (greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute). The deviation is ESTABLISHED on this trip's own trace.

The trace is clean for policy purposes: 155 fixes at a 10 second sample interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds, so POL-RD-07(a) to (c) are not met and the deviation may be established on the gps_trace alone without independent corroboration.

The rider has discharged the POL-RD-08 initial burden: the trip identifier TRP-02814 matches across the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, the pickup timestamp 2026-08-10T11:57:30+08:00 matches across the trip record and the trace, and the excess of 5.11 km / 35.00% meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace. The burden now shifts to the driver.

The driver's only explanation is 'The meter adds the extra distance.' That is a general assertion with no evidence ID and no clause invoked, so under POL-RD-08 it does not discharge the driver's burden, and under POL-RD-13 the traffic-cause route is unavailable because the only traffic advisory in the bundle is MISSING with weight 0.0 and no advisory covers this corridor.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any of the excess: the chat log for this trip carries zero messages, so there is no rider instruction, no waypoint_hint and no named road, and POL-RD-04 is unavailable on the record.

No relocation of the pickup or dropoff point can excuse the excess: both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run and the booked optimal of 14.6 km stands as the baseline.

This is an UPFRONT_QUOTE trip, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess. The rider's remedy is confined to POL-RD-11(a): the amount by which the charged total of SGD 31.80 exceeds the quoted fare of SGD 21.50 plus the properly chargeable pass-through and statutory lines. Those lines are zero here - no ERP, no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee - so the refund is SGD 10.30, which the fare breakdown itself computes as pol_rd_11_remedy.

The pass-through lines are clean and add nothing to the refund: the fare breakdown itemises zero ERP gantries, a zero airport surcharge on a trip that neither originates nor ends at an airport, and a zero waiting-time fee, so there is no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4) and no off-route ERP to refund under POL-RD-09(2).

The deviation is MATERIAL: the excess of 35.00% is below the 50% materiality percentage, but the excess of 5.11 km is below the 8.0 km materiality distance, so on the POL-RD-01 figures alone materiality is not reached. I do not overstate this - the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check is not triggered on materiality, and the driver's profile shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 against completed_trips_90d of 396, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established and no conduct referral or FULL_REFUND uplift follows.

The rider's own profile does not weaken the claim: deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the threshold of 4 that POL-RD-08 sets for requiring corroboration beyond the gps_trace on a sub-30% excess, and in any event the excess here is 35.00%, above 30%.

Under POL-RD-11(a) that excess over the quote, less only the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09, is refunded in full. The fare_breakdown's own derived money block computes pol_rd_11_remedy at 10.30, with properly_chargeable total 0.00 (no ERP lines, no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee). The rider's claim that he was quoted 21.50 and charged 31.80 is therefore correct on the platform's own ledger.

The route deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The GPS trace measures 19.71 km against a booked optimal of 14.6 km, an excess of 5.11 km and 35.00 percent. Both POL-RD-01 establishment tests pass: 35.00 percent exceeds the 20 percent threshold and 5.11 km exceeds the 0.8 km threshold. The trace figure governs over the trip_record's rounded 19.7 km copy under POL-RD-01.

The driver's only explanation is that 'the meter adds the extra distance' — a bare assertion that cites no artifact and no clause. Under POL-RD-08 the driver bears the burden once the rider has shown a matching trip and a threshold-meeting excess, and a general assertion unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID does not discharge it. No exculpatory clause is available on this record: there is no chat_log detour request (0 messages), no amendment to pickup or dropoff, and no traffic advisory.

The driver's traffic excuse is weightless. The bundle's only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-02814-01, is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload — no advisory covers the Blk 412 Pasir Ris Dr 6 corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else; with no advisory on file the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight. The deviation therefore stands at the measured figure.

The trace is clean for policy purposes, so no corroboration requirement under POL-RD-07(ii) applies. The GPS artifact is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, with 100.0 percent coverage, 155 fixes at a 10-second interval, zero gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds — none of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) impairment limbs fires. The deviation may therefore be established on the trace alone, and the rider's POL-RD-08 burden is discharged.

The deviation is MATERIAL: 35.00 percent exceeds the 50 percent materiality threshold? No — it does not, and I concede that point. The excess is 5.11 km against the 8.0 km material threshold and 35.00 percent against the 50 percent material threshold, so the deviation is established but not material, and the POL-RD-06 driver_profile pattern check is not triggered. The driver's profile is clean in any event: deviation_flags_90d is 0 over 396 completed trips in 90 days.

The rider's remedy is confined to the upfront-quote route. Because fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE, POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however large the excess; the rider is already whole on those lines. The recoverable amount is the 10.30 by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus properly chargeable pass-throughs, and the fare_breakdown's derived money block confirms pol_rd_11_remedy_available is true at 10.30.

No billing-integrity correction is due on the pass-through lines: the fare_breakdown carries zero ERP lines, zero airport surcharge and zero waiting-time fee, and the trip neither originates at an airport nor crosses a charged gantry. POL-RD-09(4) therefore has nothing to refund, and the 10.30 stands as the whole of the rider's recovery.

ruling.explanation: To both parties. Trip TRP-02814 was booked on an upfront quote, so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking. Rider: you were quoted SGD 21.50 and charged SGD 31.80. Under POL-RD-11, on an upfront-quoted trip POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available however long the route was; your remedy is the amount by which the charged total exceeds the quote plus only the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. Those lines are all zero here — no ERP gantries crossed, no airport surcharge (the trip neither originates nor ends at an airport), no waiting-time fee — so the refund is charged_total SGD 31.80 − quoted fare SGD 21.50 − properly chargeable SGD 0.00 = SGD 10.30, rounded up to the nearest 5 cents = SGD 10.30. That figure is the fare breakdown's own pol_rd_11_remedy and it is the whole of your recovery. Driver: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02814) measures 19.71 km against the booked optimal of 14.6 km, an excess of 5.11 km and 35.00%, which establishes a route deviation under POL-RD-01 — both the 20% and the 0.8 km tests pass, and the trace figure governs over the trip record's rounded 19.7 km copy. It is not a material deviation (5.11 km is below the 8.0 km and 35.00% below the 50% materiality tests), so no POL-RD-06 driver-profile check, no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral arise; the driver profile (deviation_flags_90d 0 over 396 completed 90-day trips) shows no repeat pattern in any event. The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 155 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps — so the deviation stands on the trace alone and no independent corroboration was needed. Your statement that 'the meter adds the extra distance' cites no evidence ID and invokes no clause, so under POL-RD-08 it carries no weight as an exculpation, and there is no traffic advisory on file for this trip (the bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-02814-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0), so no external-cause excuse under POL-RD-03/POL-RD-13 is available. No rider-requested detour or relocation applies: the chat log carries zero messages, so POL-RD-04 is unavailable, and no pickup or dropoff amendment was recorded, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run. The pass-through lines are clean, so POL-RD-09 yields no separate correction and no billing-integrity referral; no clause produces any referral in this case. Confidence is 0.95, below the cap of 1.0 set by the deciding artifacts (the fare breakdown and the GPS trace, each at weight 1.0). Because the monetary effect (SGD 10.30) exceeds the SGD 8.00 execution threshold, this provisional ruling is issued but held for release by a human reviewer under POL-GEN-05; either party may appeal once under POL-GEN-04.
